The edges rest on disjoint sources this batch (deliberately no within-batch shared-source provenance while the CRG redundancy-semantics question stands at eleven accumulated examples): the insomnia edge on the REST primary care study (88.4 percent sleep-symptom burden, PMID 15165529), the Sleep Heart Health home-PSG cohort (adjusted sleep latency 39.8 versus 26.4 minutes, PMID 19544754), and the REST general population study (PMID 15956009); the depressive-disorder edge on the 549-versus-549 matched-control cohort (32.5 percent depressive symptoms, 10-fold; treatment-responsive, PMID 34985142), the prospective perinatal incident-depression cohort (hazard ratio 3.04, PMID 42675332), and the 24-study pooled-prevalence meta-analysis (30.39 percent, PMID 39024776); the anxiety-disorder edge on the 21-study healthy-control meta-analysis (Beck Anxiety Inventory mean difference 9.30, zero heterogeneity, PMID 38562425), the 2,289-adolescent cohort (anxiety odds ratio 1.514, PMID 42601325), and the pregnancy case-control cohort (PMID 32676936). nexusClaim.associationBasis: Restless legs syndrome associates with disrupted sleep at multinational primary-care and population-polysomnographic level: the REST primary care study of 23,052 screened patients documents that 88.4 percent of the 551 treatment-warranting sufferers reported at least one sleep-related symptom with most reporting impaired sleep consistent with a diagnosis of insomnia and the authors concluding that restless legs syndrome often severely disrupts sleep (PMID 15165529), the Sleep Heart Health Study home-polysomnography cohort of 3,433 community participants documents longer adjusted mean sleep latency (39.8 versus 26.4 minutes, P<0.0001) and higher arousal index (20.1 versus 18.0, P=0.0145) with latency rising as symptom frequency increased, adjusted for apnea-hypopnea index and demographic and health variables (PMID 19544754), and the REST general population study of 15,391 respondents documents clinically significant restless legs syndrome in 2.7 percent with SF-36 scores significantly below population norms and sleep significantly affected (PMID 15956009); recorded as documented association only with the cross-sectional and sleep-measure limits carried openly - the polysomnographic anchor measures latency and arousal rather than a structured insomnia diagnosis and the primary-care anchor screens symptoms rather than diagnosing insomnia.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation of insomnia is established for any individual: the located anchors are cross-sectional and measure co-occurrence at one point, restless legs syndrome mimics (nocturnal leg cramps, positional discomfort, neuropathic dysesthesias) produce similar sleep disruption and inflate screening-based estimates, reverse amplification is plausible since sleep loss heightens sensory symptom perception, and the evening predominance and rest-provocation of symptoms are the defining criteria while sleep disruption itself is the dominant morbidity rather than a diagnostic criterion; individual claims require dated sleep studies or a documented insomnia diagnosis with sleep apnea (adjusted for at cohort level only), nocturnal leg cramps, medication and caffeine effects, and mood-disorder causes excluded.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Nocturnal sensorimotor symptoms - the irresistible urge to move with unpleasant dysesthesias provoked by rest and gated by evening circadian timing - are hypothesized to delay sleep onset and fragment maintenance until conditioned hyperarousal persists past the symptoms themselves, the route supported by the polysomnographic latency gradient with symptom frequency and the primary-care symptom quantification, but whether the route produced any individual's insomnia remains hypothesized until sleep and neurologic timelines are reviewed side by side.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at multinational primary-care and population-PSG class following the symptom-disrupted-sleep convention (the prurigo-nodularis to insomnia and dermatitis to insomnia family): the polysomnographic anchor objectively quantifies sleep-onset latency against non-RLS comparators with apnea-hypopnea-index adjustment (PMID 19544754), the primary-care anchor documents that most sufferers report impaired sleep consistent with a diagnosis of insomnia (PMID 15165529), and the general-population anchor quantifies the clinically significant subgroup with SF-36 impact (PMID 15956009); constitutive-proximity was screened and cleared on the record (sleep disruption is the dominant morbidity of restless legs syndrome but is not part of its diagnostic criteria); because the anchors are cross-sectional with screening- or questionnaire-defined restless legs syndrome and mimics inflate screening estimates, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only with those limits stated and routes individual claims through dated polysomnography or insomnia diagnosis with mimics excluded.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: No longitudinal incident-insomnia cohort among restless legs syndrome patients free of sleep disorder at baseline was located; the polysomnographic anchor (PMID 19544754) quantifies sleep latency and arousal index rather than an insomnia diagnosis and its restless legs syndrome definition is questionnaire-based (NIH criteria, symptoms at least five times per month); the primary-care anchor (PMID 15165529) reports symptom screens consistent with an insomnia diagnosis rather than structured insomnia diagnoses; the general-population anchor (PMID 15956009) measures SF-36 impact rather than sleep diagnoses; cross-sectional designs leave direction contested at individual level.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: obstructive sleep apnea producing sleep fragmentation with restless-leg symptoms reported secondarily (adjusted for at cohort level in the polysomnographic anchor via apnea-hypopnea index; individual claims require polysomnography)
nocturnal leg cramps, positional discomfort, and peripheral neuropathy producing mimicking restlessness and sleep disruption
mood disorders (depressive-disorder, anxiety-disorder) producing both insomnia and somatic restlessness (the registered mood windows own their sources; none recycled per ME-29)
caffeine, stimulant, and substance effects; shift-work and circadian schedule constraints

suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at multinational primary-care and population-PSG class with the cross-sectional and sleep-measure limits carried openly, following the symptom-disrupted-sleep edge convention: the REST primary care study quantifies sleep-related symptoms in 88.4 percent of treatment-warranting sufferers with most reporting impaired sleep consistent with a diagnosis of insomnia (PMID 15165529), the Sleep Heart Health Study home-PSG cohort quantifies the sleep-onset latency and arousal burden against non-RLS comparators with apnea-hypopnea-index adjustment (PMID 19544754), and the REST general population study quantifies the clinically significant subgroup with SF-36 sleep and quality-of-life impact (PMID 15956009); constitutive-proximity screened and cleared (sleep disruption is the dominant morbidity but not a diagnostic criterion of restless legs syndrome); because all three anchors are cross-sectional with questionnaire-defined restless legs syndrome and mimics inflate screening estimates, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only with those limits on the record and routes individual claims through dated polysomnography or insomnia diagnosis with sleep apnea, leg cramps, and mood causes excluded.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Restless legs syndrome associates with depressive morbidity at matched-control and prospective-cohort level: the case-control cohort of 549 untreated patients versus 549 age-, sex-, and education-matched controls documents depressive symptoms in 32.5 percent (10-fold higher than controls) with current major depressive episode in 10.5 percent of the interviewed subgroup and moderate-to-severe depressive symptoms associated with insomnia symptoms and with RLS severity and improving with restless legs syndrome treatment (PMID 34985142), the prospective cohort of 2,435 Japanese pregnant women documents time-varying restless legs syndrome associated with incident perinatal depression (hazard ratio 3.04, 95 percent CI 1.22-7.58) and incident depressive symptoms (Edinburgh scale at least 13, hazard ratio 2.12, 95 percent CI 1.28-3.51) robust to confounder adjustment (PMID 42675332), and the systematic review and meta-analysis of 24 studies with 2,039 patients documents pooled depression or depressive-state prevalence of 30.39 percent (PMID 39024776); recorded as documented association only with an explicit null counterweight carried openly - a pregnancy case-control cohort documented no depression-score difference between restless legs syndrome and control pregnant women (P=0.269) despite a positive anxiety signal in the same sample (PMID 32676936, registered on the anxiety-disorder edge within this batch) - and the intermediate-node limit is carried (depressive symptoms track insomnia symptoms in the matched-control anchor and the registered insomnia to depressive-disorder window exists).
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation of depressive-disorder is established for any individual: the sleep-disruption route is an intermediate-node candidate (insomnia symptoms tracked the depressive symptoms in the matched-control anchor and the registered insomnia to depressive-disorder edge owns that route), the prospective anchor is perinatal-scoped with pregnancy-specific iron deficiency and hormonal substrate, reverse direction is documented in the wider mood literature (antidepressant treatment can precipitate or worsen restless legs symptoms and depression commonly precedes somatic symptom amplification), shared dopaminergic and iron substrate drives both conditions, and one located case-control cohort found no depression difference (P=0.269); individual claims require dated psychiatric assessment with pre-existing mood disorder, medication effects including antidepressants and dopamine antagonists, iron deficiency, and adjustment disorder excluded.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Chronic nocturnal discomfort with relentless sleep-onset and maintenance disruption is hypothesized to erode mood regulation over time, while shared dopaminergic and iron-deficiency substrate and the insomnia pathway run alongside the route as competing or mediating paths, the forward route supported by the matched-control symptom quantification and the prospective incident-depression hazard ratios with restless legs syndrome treatment improving depressive symptoms in the treated subgroup, but whether the forward route produced any individual's depressive episode remains hypothesized until psychiatric and neurologic timelines are reviewed side by side.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at matched-control plus prospective-cohort class with the null counterweight and intermediate-node limits carried openly, following the PSYCHOPHYSIOLOGICAL mood-edge convention: the 549-versus-549 matched-control cohort quantifies the depressive-symptom and major-depressive-episode burden with treatment response (PMID 34985142), the prospective perinatal cohort quantifies incident depression after time-varying restless legs syndrome with temporal order (PMID 42675332), and the meta-analysis quantifies pooled prevalence across 24 studies (PMID 39024776); the pregnancy case-control depression null (P=0.269, PMID 32676936) is carried openly as explicit counterweight and its source is registered on the anxiety-disorder edge within this batch; because the sleep-mediation route is documented within the anchor itself and the prospective anchor is perinatal-scoped, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only with those limits stated and routes individual claims through dated psychiatric, neurologic, and sleep timelines with pre-existing mood disorder and iron deficiency excluded.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: No general-population longitudinal incident-depression cohort among restless legs syndrome patients free of mood disorder at baseline was located (the located prospective anchor is perinatal-scoped); the matched-control anchor is clinic-based with questionnaire depression screens plus a structured-interview subgroup; the meta-analysis pools mostly questionnaire-defined depressive states; the depression signal tracks insomnia symptoms within the matched-control anchor (mediation not resolved); and one pregnancy case-control cohort found no depression-score difference (P=0.269) with the counterweight carried openly.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: pre-existing depressive-disorder antedating the sensorimotor syndrome (individual claims require documented pre-morbid psychiatric history)
insomnia-mediated mood morbidity (the registered insomnia to depressive-disorder window owns its sources; none recycled per ME-29)
iron deficiency and dopaminergic dysfunction as shared substrate driving both conditions
antidepressant and dopamine-antagonist medication effects precipitating or amplifying restlessness (reverse direction); substance use including alcohol and nicotine

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Restless legs syndrome associates with anxiety symptoms at healthy-control meta-analytic and case-control level: the systematic review and meta-analysis of 21 studies documents significantly more pronounced anxiety in restless legs syndrome than in healthy controls on the Beck Anxiety Inventory (mean difference 9.30, 95 percent CI 7.65-10.94, P<0.01, heterogeneity I-squared 0 percent) with all other anxiety scales also significant (PMID 38562425), the school-adolescent cross-sectional cohort of 2,289 participants documents higher anxiety risk with restless legs syndrome (odds ratio 1.514, P<0.001) alongside higher depression (odds ratio 1.678) and stress scores with mood derangements higher in both younger and older adolescent strata (PMID 42601325), and the pregnancy case-control study of 119 versus 134 pregnant women documents higher Beck Anxiety Inventory scores in the restless legs syndrome group (P<0.001) with anxiety scores correlating with syndrome severity in both groups (P<0.001) (PMID 32676936); recorded as documented association only with the shared-substrate and scale-measure limits carried openly - the pregnancy cohort attributes part of the association to magnesium and zinc deficiency and documents a null depression comparison (P=0.269) in the same sample.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation of anxiety-disorder is established for any individual: the anchors are symptom-scale based (Beck Anxiety Inventory and questionnaire mood scales rather than structured anxiety diagnoses), two of three anchors are special-population scoped (school adolescents, pregnant women) where anxiety physiology overlaps the somatic state (pregnancy discomfort, adolescent circadian and academic stress), the direction is contested (anxious arousal can mimic and amplify nocturnal restlessness and anxiety scores correlate with syndrome severity within the pregnancy cohort), shared substrate (magnesium and zinc deficiency in the pregnancy cohort; dopaminergic and iron substrate generally) drives both directions, and autonomic arousal of anxiety overlaps the sensory symptoms; individual claims require dated psychiatric assessment with pre-existing anxiety disorder, stimulant and caffeine effects, thyroid disease, and adjustment disorder excluded.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Anticipatory anxiety about nocturnal symptoms and the conditioned hypervigilance of sleep-onset restlessness are hypothesized to generalize into sustained anxiety symptoms over time while shared mineral and dopaminergic substrate and anxious arousal amplifying restlessness run the coupling in reverse as well, the forward route supported by the zero-heterogeneity meta-analytic anxiety-score excess and the adolescent odds ratio with cross-stratum consistency, but whether the forward route produced any individual's anxiety disorder remains hypothesized until psychiatric and neurologic timelines are reviewed side by side.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at healthy-control meta-analytic plus case-control class with the shared-substrate, scale-measure, and special-population limits carried openly, following the PSYCHOPHYSIOLOGICAL mood-edge convention: the 21-study meta-analysis quantifies the anxiety-score excess against healthy controls with zero heterogeneity on the Beck Anxiety Inventory (PMID 38562425), the 2,289-adolescent cohort quantifies the anxiety odds ratio with age-stratum consistency (PMID 42601325), and the pregnancy case-control cohort quantifies the anxiety-score excess with severity correlation (PMID 32676936); the same pregnancy cohort's null depression comparison (P=0.269) is carried openly as counterweight (registered within this batch on this edge); because the anchors use symptom scales in special populations with contested direction and shared mineral substrate, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only with those limits stated and routes individual claims through dated psychiatric timelines with pre-existing anxiety disorder and substance effects excluded.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: No general-population longitudinal incident-anxiety cohort among restless legs syndrome patients free of anxiety at baseline was located; the meta-analysis pools symptom-scale scores (Beck Anxiety Inventory primary; Hamilton-scale results heterogeneous) rather than structured anxiety diagnoses and frames the evidence base as controversial at protocol entry; the adolescent and pregnancy anchors are special-population scoped; the pregnancy anchor attributes part of the association to magnesium and zinc deficiency (shared substrate unresolved); and the anxiety-severity correlation leaves direction contested.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: pre-existing anxiety disorder antedating the sensorimotor syndrome (individual claims require documented pre-morbid psychiatric history)
anxious arousal and hypervigilance mimicking or amplifying nocturnal restlessness (direction contested)
magnesium and zinc deficiency and iron deficiency as shared substrate (documented in the pregnancy cohort)
stimulant, caffeine, and thyroid-related hyperarousal states; adolescent and pregnancy-specific physiologic and psychosocial stressors
sleep-loss-mediated anxiety symptoms (the registered insomnia windows own their sources; none recycled per ME-29)

evidenceGaps: No general-population longitudinal incident-anxiety cohort among restless legs syndrome patients free of anxiety at baseline was located; the meta-analysis pools symptom-scale scores (Beck Anxiety Inventory primary; Hamilton-scale results heterogeneous) rather than structured anxiety diagnoses and frames the evidence base as controversial at protocol entry; the adolescent and pregnancy anchors are special-population scoped; the pregnancy anchor attributes part of the association to magnesium and zinc deficiency (shared substrate unresolved); and the anxiety-severity correlation leaves direction contested.
